feedback:
Reviewed before racing, so no outcome is stated for this candidate. It changes one value from the best raced design (iteration 8, score 686.6): controller.base_speed 1.2 to 1.4. Sensor geometry (all five sensors at y 0.06, x -0.03 to 0.03, size 0.016), kp 1.5, ki 0.02, kd 0.6, sensor_weights and line_loss last_direction are unchanged, so any result is attributable to speed. All fields are within the contract ranges.

The evidence supports this step. In iteration 8 the oval and s-bend finished 20 of 20 with mean times of about 2.0 s and 2.2 s, which leaves headroom under the 3 s limit and gives the time term (60*(1 - t/3)) something to gain. Slalom ended off track in 20 of 20 runs in iteration 8, and its progress rose from 0.33 to 0.40 when the sensors moved to y 0.06. Iterations 4 to 7 showed that slalom line loss did not respond to kp, kd or line_loss direction, so speed is the remaining untested lever with a plausible effect on the completed tracks.

The main risks are that the faster robot leaves the track sooner on the tight slalom bends, that the 2 percent motor mismatch and sensor noise matter more at higher speed, and that the final unseen track may be harder than the development tracks. The gain on the finished tracks is modest (roughly 6 points per track from the time term), so a loss of even one finish costs far more than the speed gain adds. Read the race as follows. If oval or s-bend finishes fall below 18 of 20, or slalom progress falls below 0.33, revert base_speed to 1.2. If steering_oscillation on the s-bend or oval rises above 0.4, revert too. If all finishes hold and completion_time drops clearly on the oval and s-bend, keep 1.4 as the new best and consider a small further step only if slalom progress also rises.
requested_changes: If oval or s-bend finishes fall below 18 of 20, or slalom progress falls below 0.33, revert controller.base_speed to 1.2 with sensors at y 0.06, because the faster robot is leaving the track more often than the time term can repay.

If s-bend or oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.4 without a fall in slalom line_loss_events, revert controller.base_speed to 1.2 and keep the iteration 8 design, since the iteration 8 s-bend and oval oscillation (0.31 and 0.24) leave little room at higher speed.

If all finishes hold and completion_time drops on the oval and s-bend with slalom progress at or above 0.40, keep base_speed 1.4 as the new best and test controller.kd 0.7 as a single guard step, so the damping can be checked against the higher speed.
